citation: John Carbutt, '70. Lake street, East from Clark.' Stereograph from Carbutt's Views of Chicago, c. 1866-1871. New York Public Library, Robert N. Dennis collection of stereoscopic views, 'Stereoscopic views of streets in Chicago', MFY Dennis Coll 90-F179 (digital ID G90F179_027F).
author: John Carbutt, photographer, Chicago
repository: New York Public Library, Miriam and Ira D. Wallach Division of Art, Prints and Photographs: Photography Collection; catalog record b11707456.
locator: Lake Street's business blocks east from Clark: attached four- and five-storey fronts party wall to party wall, segmental-headed windows in hooded surrounds under bracketed cornices, painted wall signs and lettered signboards (CAPS & FURS among them), canvas awnings over the walk.
rights_note: Created before 1871; public domain. NYPL marks the Dennis collection 'No known copyright restrictions'. Read for period forms only; no pixels are sampled and no geometry is traced.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-19 (T-3686) from NYPL's image server, digital ID G90F179_027F.
note: A street view, not a survey: it shows how the pre-fire business streets and residential blocks were built, not the fronts of the generated lots.
what_it_supplies: attached commercial rows of four and five storeys on Lake Street, without side gaps
segmental and round-headed windows with hoods, bracketed cornices, painted signboards and wall lettering, awnings
cast-iron and glazed ground-floor shop fronts
what_it_does_not_supply: the identity, width or height of any generated front
sign wording for any particular building
